title: Week 4 Mastery Quiz · Political Ideologies and Models of Justice

questions.question: Fictional policy platform: 'Freedom means minimal government restriction on voluntary exchange.' Which tension should an analyst test?
options: Market freedom and bargaining power can be compared solely by counting regulations.
If exchange is voluntary by law, unequal bargaining conditions cannot affect choice.
How market freedom interacts with unequal bargaining power and collective obligations
Collective obligations are definitionally excluded from any defensible account of liberty.
questions.explanation: How market freedom interacts with unequal bargaining power and collective obligations

questions.question: Two fictional housing proposals both claim fairness: one gives equal grants; the other varies grants by household need. What is the clearest comparative question?
options: Which politician smiles more
How each defines equality, need, costs, and the criteria for just allocation
Which label sounds more persuasive
Whether they use the same font
questions.explanation: How each defines equality, need, costs, and the criteria for just allocation

questions.question: A speech calls a policy 'traditional' but provides no historical evidence. What should a source critic do?
options: Treat tradition as proof of effectiveness
Reject every inherited practice
Use only the speaker's party label
Identify the claimed tradition, trace historical records, and separately evaluate policy consequences
questions.explanation: Identify the claimed tradition, trace historical records, and separately evaluate policy consequences

questions.question: Simulated fiscal plan: a universal benefit costs 12 units, a targeted benefit 7 units, and available funds equal 10. Which judgment respects both evidence and values?
options: Compare fiscal feasibility and the stated equity criteria rather than declaring one policy morally proven by cost alone
The universal plan is feasible without changes
Targeting is always unjust
Cost figures have no bearing on policy
questions.explanation: Compare fiscal feasibility and the stated equity criteria rather than declaring one policy morally proven by cost alone

questions.question: A fictional environmental coalition supports conservation but disagrees about carbon-tax rebates. What comparison best clarifies the disagreement?
options: Membership counts alone
Only their logos
Their distributional assumptions, expected emissions effects, and definitions of a fair transition
Whether all members use the term green
questions.explanation: Their distributional assumptions, expected emissions effects, and definitions of a fair transition

questions.question: A manifesto advocates strong national identity while formally guaranteeing minority cultural rights. What must the student investigate before classification?
options: Assume the guarantee is enforced
Compare the text, implementation, and competing accounts of rights and membership
Treat every nationalist movement as identical
Ignore the rights clause
questions.explanation: Compare the text, implementation, and competing accounts of rights and membership

questions.question: Fictional legal memo: 'The law applies uniformly,' but enforcement records show district-level disparities. What tension appears?
options: No tension
The law was never written
Only a terminology problem
Formal equality versus unequal administration, requiring explanation of the observed differences
questions.explanation: Formal equality versus unequal administration, requiring explanation of the observed differences

questions.question: Two commentators dispute whether public childcare promotes liberty. Which comparison demonstrates senior-level reasoning?
options: State each conception of freedom, affected groups, opportunity costs, and the evidence each relies upon
Choose the louder commentator
Treat all value claims as scientific facts
Ignore fiscal feasibility
questions.explanation: State each conception of freedom, affected groups, opportunity costs, and the evidence each relies upon

questions.question: A political pamphlet from 1905 and a modern platform share the term socialism but differ in property and governance proposals. What is the safest interpretation?
options: The term has an unchanging policy definition
Their programs must be identical
Compare period-specific proposals rather than treating the shared label as sufficient evidence
Neither text may be interpreted
questions.explanation: Compare period-specific proposals rather than treating the shared label as sufficient evidence

questions.question: A proposal appeals simultaneously to national solidarity, gender equality, and environmental protection. Which research method avoids forcing a false single label?
options: Choose only the first value mentioned
Map its separate commitments, policy mechanisms, tensions, and institutional consequences
Ignore all internal contradictions
Assign ideology from the party color
questions.explanation: Map its separate commitments, policy mechanisms, tensions, and institutional consequences

shortResponse: How do political ideologies define freedom, equality, authority, property, obligation, and justice?
rubric: 10 points: precise claim (2), accurate concepts (2), two specific pieces of evidence (2), reasoning (2), counterargument or limitation (1), revision condition (1).
